original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: For the four-role target diag([A+P],[A+Q],[B+P],[B+Q]) of PR #2085 and the five-address alphabet {A,B,P,Q,R_t}, R_t=(1,t)^T(1,t), with paid factors I+([F]-1)N over all rank-one idempotents N in M4(F2), determine the exact paid-call minimum for every rational t. This settles the seven-call case left open by PR #2112 at t=1/2.
scope_change_reason: The card permits a specified legal operation alphabet. This keeps the four roles, target and model of PRs #2085/#2112 and answers their stated open questions (the R_t slope family and the seven-call case) instead of searching a new alphabet.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the bit primitive in a favorable formal paid-call model: it removes one candidate saving route (a fifth symmetric rank-one frame) for this target. The selected result's complex primitive still binds; no supplier or kappa change follows.
stop_rule: Stop once the exact minimum is decided for every rational t; do not extend to scaled frames or two added frames in this session.
evidence: Exponent support: each target frame must equal a nonnegative subset sum of the word's labels; with at most seven calls R_t can enter such a sum only at t=0, so for t!=0 each of A,B,P,Q is used. First order: for odd-denominator t, L/2L is the old lattice mod 2 and R_t is A or 0, giving the PR #2085 floor 8 at every length. For even-denominator t, B lies in 2L, A,P,R_t give a basis mod 2, and a word using R_t needs an even number (>=2) of R_t calls, at least one B call and at least 5 A/P/Q calls (exact minimum over 65,536 masks), so at least 8. The direct eight-call word attains 8.

open_questions.question: Can a scaled rational rank-one address c v^T v, or a pair of added frames, lower the eight-call minimum for this target?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This package closes only the one-parameter slope family R_t; the support step suggests that only addresses entering a target's exponent support can matter.
open_questions.first_step: Classify the addresses that can appear in a nonnegative support of a target frame using at most seven calls, then apply the first-order floor to those alone.
open_questions.blocked_by: Two added frames can make target supports non-unique, so the forced-label count used here no longer follows.

open_questions.question: Does exponent support plus the first-order floor decide other open minimum-length cases in torsion-free address models?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It replaces word enumeration by a small exact computation when target supports are unique.
open_questions.first_step: Apply the two screens to a recorded open minimum-length case with a torsion-free address group.
open_questions.blocked_by: Targets with several supports and finite (torsion) address groups, where the support step is weaker.
